source_blocks.text: We report a prodrug-conjugated polymer platform for controlled drug delivery. The polymer backbone is synthesized by reversible addition-fragmentation chain-transfer polymerization of a methacrylate monomer bearing a hydrolytically cleavable doxorubicin conjugate. The resulting amphiphilic block copolymer self-assembles into nanoparticles with a hydrodynamic diameter of approximately 120 nanometers and a low critical micelle concentration.

The drug loading content was determined by ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy to be 18.5 percent, with an encapsulation efficiency of 72 percent. Release kinetics in phosphate-buffered saline at pH 7.4 showed a cumulative release of 65 percent over 72 hours, consistent with ester-bond hydrolysis of the linker.

In vitro cytotoxicity assays against HeLa cells demonstrated that the polymer-drug conjugate exhibited comparable activity to the free drug after 48 hours of incubation, while the blank polymer remained non-toxic at the tested concentrations.

metadata.title: Prodrug-conjugated polymer nanoparticles for controlled doxorubicin delivery
